# Selecting Element

#### Course: JavaScript in Browser

## Selecting Element

You can use the querySelector() method to select the element.

```html
1<header id="header">
2    <div id="logo">E-Commerce</div>
3    <nav>
4        <ul class="nav-links">
5            <li><a href="#home">Home</a></li>
6            <li><a href="#products">Products</a></li>
7            <li><a href="#contact">Contact</a></li>
8        </ul>
9    </nav>
10</header>
11
12<div class="hero">
13    <h1>Welcome to our store</h1>
14    <p>Discover the best deals on your favorite products.</p>
15    <button class="button">Shop Now</button>
16</div>
```

```javascript
1const logo = document.querySelector("#logo");
2
3console.log(logo);
```

Console Output

![Selecting Element](data:image/png;base64,)

Here, querySelector("#logo") selects the element with the id logo, which is the logo itself.

As you can see in the console output, selecting the logo accesses its entire HTML structure, including its content.

![Idea Emoji](data:image/png;base64,)
